resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1935-36 newspapers name the Forest Service as builder and the Register names it as administrator; the historical marker credits the CCC with building the tower in 1935. The sources do not say how the two relate, so the story reports both.

The Register visit found no access and no-trespassing signs at the tower; the Forest Service trail page invites hikers up the Tower trail toward it. Both are reported; the tower itself is treated as closed.

notes_for_editor: Built date, design and Forest Service use are well supported by the Register and 1935-36 newspapers as quoted on the Forest Lookouts site. Open points: (1) the Forest Lookouts site gives the tower's location about 2 km from the Register's coordinates (34.10012, -82.35429 vs 34.08306, -82.36278); the record keeps the Register point, which was not checked on a map. (2) Elevation differs: the Register gives 824 ft, the marker gives 832 ft for the mountain, and the Forest Service page says an 800-foot mound. (3) The Forest Service trail page's Hurricane Helene closure note sits under a 'Current Conditions' heading, and the page's last-updated date is April 22, 2026; access today should be confirmed before any visit. (4) The access level 'closed' is inferred from the 2020 visit notes, not from a current agency notice. Visit report and fence observations are from one 2020 volunteer visit.
